A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and are readable throughout, including their equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The retained methods and experiments can be matched reliably despite substantial theoretical rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on six long-context tasks, including model comparisons, chunk-size sweeps, prompt comparisons, and supplementary evaluations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results in the main text and appendices. Results retained from v1 still constitute original empirical evidence.

M1.justification: The planner–worker–manager pipeline, chunk processing, prompts, and refinement procedure are retained. The sparse chunk-size selection described in v2 Sections 4 and 5.5 already appears in v1 Appendix F. The new fidelity losses reformulate the analysis without changing inference or training.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate KV retrieval, Math, QA-IB, QA-LB, summarization, and character inference using the same modified InfiniteBench and LongBench-V2 coverage. V2 Appendix D relocates the existing task descriptions.

E2.justification: The evaluated model sets, single-shot comparisons, BM25/mpnet RAG baselines, and RoPE-extension comparisons are retained. LOGO, LongReward, and LongPO are newly cited as related work but are not added to the reported experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: The experiments retain their accuracy/F1/ROUGE metrics, context and chunk-size grids, model configurations, temperature-zero decoding, one planner refinement, and 3/5/10-document search budgets. V2 clarifies the existing sampling procedure and reframes the diagnostic curves without establishing changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: The prompt comparisons, sparse-search analysis, overlap tests, context-extension tests, and diverse-model evaluations already appear in v1. V2's new cost and segmentation appendices provide analytical arguments and explanations, without adding ablations, robustness tests, or empirical case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The retained 3/5/10-document sampling budgets concern chunk-size selection, not repeated-run uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V1 Tables 1–8 retain their numerical entries in v2 Tables 2–9, and Figures 2–4 retain identical plot content. V2 Table 1 combines the existing sparse-search results from v1 Tables 3–4; it introduces no new outcomes.

T1.justification: V2 replaces the product-of-outputs noise framework with score-ratio fidelity definitions and an exact additive logarithmic-loss decomposition. It introduces positivity and monotonicity assumptions, replaces Assumption 3.1/Theorem 3.2 and their appendices with a conditional linear-versus-superlinear loss argument, and derives the high-fidelity approximation. Appendix N also adds latency and monetary-cost equations.

C1.justification: The three principal contributions remain: explaining when chunking helps, showing weaker models can outperform stronger single-shot models, and improving coordination through prompts. However, the abstract and contribution list soften the empirical growth claim from superlinear noise/degradation to accelerated fidelity decay/degradation, and the conclusion adopts the revised fidelity-loss formulation.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly distinguishes empirical proxies from unobservable decomposition terms and explains task loss as an information bottleneck under a fixed output schema. New Appendices N–O substantially expand applicability discussions: efficiency depends on concurrency and short worker outputs, while fixed-length chunking controls confounding factors that adaptive segmentation would change.

D1.justification: V2 documents the existing sparse-search procedure more precisely, including its development set, sampling without replacement, score averaging, and selection rule. It also removes v1's opening footnote promising code release and providing a repository URL. The PDFs do not establish an actual change in repository availability.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds LOGO, LongReward, and LongPO as complementary approaches based on preference or reward optimization. Section 2.3 removes the specific criticism that prior coordination mechanisms lack principled worker–manager balancing. The broader positioning against existing divide-and-conquer methods remains.

P1.justification: Section 3 and the conclusion are substantially rewritten, and terminology and experimental explanations are revised throughout. Task descriptions move to Appendix D, sparse-search material gains dedicated main-text treatment, and the appendices are reorganized and expanded with authorship disclosure, efficiency analysis, and segmentation rationale.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn to show planner connections to both workers and manager. V2 adds a combined main-text table displaying existing results, revises captions, relocates figures, and adopts conference headers and typography. The performance plots and existing table structures are largely preserved.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially improves the central theoretical contribution. It replaces v1's unsupported growth-rate elimination and conflicting asymptotic chunk-count bounds with explicit fidelity definitions and a clearer conditional loss-scaling argument (Section 3 and Appendices B–C). The proxy qualifications and deployment caveats further improve interpretability. The unchanged experiments do not directly validate the new assumptions, and removing the code-release link modestly weakens reproducibility information, but these limitations do not outweigh the theoretical improvement.
